messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — tool-call failures observed for tenant 'cascade-health' in their Dedicated VPC. Error spike at 20:07 UTC, 5xx from parser service. Paging on-call.
Megan Li: I'm on it. seeing errors in the aggregator: ~90% of /v1/tool-call responses return 502 with 'parser_error' since 20:07.
Megan Li: Quick impact check — this tenant is on a dedicated pool (dedicated-us-west-2-cascade). Looks isolated to that pool so far.
Rajesh Kumar: pulling logs. initial suspicion: recent runtime bump (runtime-agent 2.3.1) rolled to that pool yesterday. might be a parser change.
Oliver Park: I can repro locally against a snapshot of their model routing. getting JSON parse failure in toolcall parser: `Unexpected token ':' at pos 648` for a field that used to be optional.
Megan Li: tagging @deploy-bot to see rollout history.
deploy-bot: rollout-history: runtime-agent 2.3.1 -> ded-pool-cascade @ 2025-03-09T18:12:03Z by release/2.3.1. No canary configured for that pool (manual pin override).
Rajesh Kumar: ok, looks like the runtime now enforces stricter tool-call output schemas (it rejects extra trailing commas and requires `metadata` object to be present). Cascade's toolchain emits a slightly different shape. Parser regression.
Tess K.: I've opened a line with the customer and they report tool calls failing from their app. They need ETA.
Megan Li: short mitigation plan: 1) route tenant to compatibility parser (parser-legacy) in that pool, 2) if routing not possible quickly, rollback runtime to 2.3.0 for that pool, 3) communicate to customer.
Rajesh Kumar: trying toggle now.
Rajesh Kumar: ran: ```
# enable legacy parser for cascade tenant in pool
redwood-admin set-tenant-flag --tenant cascade-health --pool dedicated-us-west-2-cascade --flag parser_mode=legacy
```
Rajesh Kumar: API accepted. Monitoring...
Oliver Park: logs show retries dropping, error rate falling from 92% -> 12% within 2m. woo.
Megan Li: Tess, can you confirm Cascade sees improvement?
Tess K.: customer confirms toolcalls partially back. Some older requests still erroring due to cached KV entries.
SRE-Chris: I'll flush the cache for the tenant KV store to speed recovery: ```
# flush tenant KV for cascade
redwood-kvctl flush --tenant cascade-health --namespace toolcall-cache
```
SRE-Chris: flush done. Customer reports almost all flows recovered.
Tess K.: customer appreciative, asks for root cause and next steps.
Rajesh Kumar: root cause summary for now: parser regression introduced in runtime-agent 2.3.1 tightened schema enforcement; customer payloads included an optional field that is now required/validated differently. Because the tenant is on a dedicated pool, the rollout hit them directly (manual pin/cfg prevented canary).
Megan Li: action items: - Rajesh to prepare a short rollback or patch (priority). - Release to add a canary gating check for dedicated pools. - Product to review 'parser_mode' as a per-tenant safety flag. - Tess to send a customer-facing incident note.
Rajesh Kumar: starting rollback to 2.3.0 for dedicated-us-west-2-cascade (targeted). Command: ```
redwood-deploy rollback --pool dedicated-us-west-2-cascade --to-tag runtime-agent@2.3.0 --reason "parser regressed on tool-call schema"
```
deploy-bot: rollback job queued (job id 88421). ETA ~7m for rolling restart across pool.
Megan Li: switching to monitoring channel, handoff to SRE-Chris for post-rollback watch. I'll stay active for customer comms.
SRE-Chris: I'm watching metrics and tailing logs. If rollback goes green we'll keep parser_mode=legacy for 24h and then coordinate patch.
SRE-Chris: rollback completed. Error rate down to baseline ~0.4% for the pool. :white_check_mark:
Tess K.: sent customer message: "We mitigated the issue by routing you to a compatibility parser and rolling back a runtime change. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with proposed permanent fix and timeline." They asked for a followup call tomorrow.
Rajesh Kumar: next steps for engineering: 1) create hotfix branch to relax strict validation OR add opt-in validator flags, 2) add dedicated-pool canary enforcement (don't allow force-rollouts without approval), 3) write test cases that include customer's payload shapes (Tess please prod samples).
Megan Li: logging ticket  #INC-2025-3248 created and linked to the thread. Jess from product added to review gating.
Oliver Park: one more note: we should add a telemetry check — when parser errors > 5% for a single tenant in a pool, auto-enable legacy parser and page oncall. prevents customer-visible break for schema drift.
SRE-Chris: agreed. I'll create monitoring alert and a runbook update.
Megan Li: handoff summary: incident mitigated by tenant flag + rollback. Impact: Cascade Health experienced ~90% tool-call failures for ~12 minutes, scoped to their dedicated pool only, no cross-tenant exposure. Root cause: stricter parser validation in runtime-agent 2.3.1. Owners: Rajesh (fix/patch), SRE-Chris (monitoring/runbook), Tess (customer comms), Megan (post-mortem).
Megan Li: tagging for postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Please gather logs, CI diffs for 2.3.1, and the customer's sample payloads.
incident-bot: Incident P1 (ID: P1-2025-3248) transitioned to 'mitigated' at 20:31 UTC.
Megan Li: closing thread here; reopen if anything regresses. :heart:
